criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust â€” no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a new request, when it is submitted, then it is recorded in the system.
Given an Excel report, when it is uploaded, then the system analyzes it to identify business objectives and scope.
Trust: Given an analysis, when it is completed, then it is logged with a timestamp and analyst ID.
Given a new request, when it is logged, then the system tracks its lifecycle stages.
Given a request update, when it is processed, then the system updates the status and history.
Trust: The system maintains an audit trail of status changes.

stories.notes: Adds a lifecycle status field (intake/analyzed/analysis_failed/completed) with an explicit transition map enforcing controlled status changes (illegal moves such as completed->intake are rejected; same-status calls are idempotent no-ops), a PATCH /requests/<id>/status endpoint for updates, a GET /requests/<id> endpoint returning current status plus the full chronological audit trail, and durable SQLite-backed audit entries for every status change.

criteria.text: Given an unclear requirement, when it is detected, then the system generates follow-up questions.
Given a complete requirement, when it is reviewed, then no follow-up questions are generated.
Trust: The system logs all clarification interactions in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Adds deterministic missing-field detection (src/requirement_clarification.py) over the seven fields analyze_email()/analyze_report() already extract, a POST /requests/<id>/clarify endpoint that returns one follow-up question per missing field (empty list when complete), and an audit entry for every clarification call via a new RequestIntake.record_clarification(). Split the audit log out of request_intake.py into src/audit_trail.py because request_intake.py was already over this repo's 200-line file cap before this change. Also fixed a pre-existing key mismatch in src/excel_analysis.py ('objectives' vs 'business_objectives') that would have broken clarification for Excel-sourced requests.

criteria.text: Given an Excel report, when it is uploaded, then the system maps fields to approved tables.
Given a field with no mapping, when it is processed, then the system flags it for review.
Trust: The system logs all mapping actions in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Maps uploaded report headers (.xlsx/.xlsm via openpyxl, plus .csv) to this repo's one existing approved schema -- REQUIRED_FIELDS from src/email_analysis.py (business_objectives, scope, kpis, filters, calculations, visual_requirements, reporting_expectations), the same fields excel_analysis.py and requirement_clarification.py already validate against; no richer table/column schema exists yet (that's STORY-005+). Unmatched headers are returned in a 'flagged' list rather than silently dropped, unlike excel_analysis.py's own header scan. New POST /requests/field-mapping endpoint follows the submit_excel_request() pattern (reject bad extension before creating a request; mark analysis_failed-style only for a corrupt/empty file after creation). Routes live in a new src/field_mapping_routes.py rather than inline in app.py, which was already at 197 of this repo's 200-line cap (same reason STORY-003 split audit_trail.py out of request_intake.py). Extended RequestIntake.record_clarification() with an optional error_category param (default None, existing callers/tests unchanged) and reused it as-is for field-mapping audit events rather than adding a near-duplicate method, since request_intake.py had only ~17 lines of headroom left. openpyxl was already in requirements.txt from STORY-001. Also includes a `python -m src.field_mapping <path>` CLI entry point for running the mapping directly without the Flask server. Also has a separate, disconnected prototype in docs/Assignment_1/scripts/field_mapping.py from earlier in this session (against an unrelated made-up KB schema) -- superseded by this src/ implementation and not part of this verification.

Trust: Given AI-generated recommendations, when they are created, then they are logged for review.

criteria.text: Given a design recommendation, when processed, then the system generates a dashboard mockup.
Given a mockup, when reviewed, then it matches the approved template.
Trust: The system logs mockup generation in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Generates a dashboard mockup (pages + visuals) from an already-generated STORY-005 design recommendation, supplied directly in the request payload since recommendations aren't persisted on the request record. src/dashboard_mockup_template.py defines the approved template as its own deterministic contract (APPROVED_VISUAL_TYPES plus shape/compliance checks) so 'matches the approved template' is independently testable from AI-call orchestration in src/dashboard_mockup.py. Every outcome (missing data, generated, template mismatch, model/API failure) writes an audit entry; if that audit write itself fails (sqlite3.Error), the new route returns a controlled 500 audit_log_unavailable instead of crashing or silently treating the outcome as logged -- a fix scoped to this route only, not a refactor of the older AI-assisted routes. commit_sha/commit_url/commit_at are left null in this verification: a commit cannot correctly record its own resulting hash inside itself, so those three fields are filled by a short follow-up commit once this one's real hash is known (same pattern as STORY-005's commit_sha being filled in after the fact by 2b61456).

criteria.text: Given a dashboard mockup, when processed, then the system generates a draft Power BI solution.
Given a draft solution, when reviewed, then it aligns with the mockup.
Trust: The system logs draft generation in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Generates a draft Power BI solution (pages + visuals + field_bindings) from an already-generated STORY-006 dashboard mockup, supplied directly in the request payload since mockups aren't persisted on the request record. src/powerbi_solution_template.py reuses STORY-006's APPROVED_VISUAL_TYPES and adds find_mockup_alignment_violations(), a positional diff against the specific source mockup (page titles/order, visual types/order) -- the testable meaning of 'aligns with the mockup', distinct from STORY-006's fixed-template check. The input mockup's own shape is re-validated (reusing dashboard_mockup_template.validate_mockup_shape()) before any model call. Same audit-per-outcome and audit_log_unavailable 500 guard pattern as STORY-006. commit_sha/commit_url/commit_at were filled in by a short follow-up commit once 00c419c's real hash was known, same as STORY-005's commit_sha being filled in after the fact by 2b61456.

criteria.text: Given a draft, when it is ready for review, then stakeholders can access it.
Given a draft, when a stakeholder requests changes, then the system logs the request.
Trust: Given a draft, when it is approved, then it is logged with the approver's ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Adds review/approval lifecycle stages (in_review, changes_requested, approved) to src/lifecycle.py; persists draft_solution on the request record via a new src/request_schema.py (split out of request_intake.py, which was already at the 200-line cap once submit_draft_for_review needed to land); adds src/stakeholder_review.py (submit_draft_for_review, approve, request_changes) and src/stakeholder_review_routes.py (POST /requests/<id>/submit-for-review, POST /requests/<id>/review). Stakeholder access is the existing GET /requests/<id> endpoint, which now returns draft_solution once submitted. approve() is the only code path that can set status to approved -- no AI-calling code in this pipeline reaches it -- satisfying REQ-012's human-approval gate. request_changes() requires non-empty feedback, stored in the audit entry's existing error_category column (reused, not a new column, same pattern as STORY-004's field-mapping audit entries).

criteria.text: Given a draft solution, when validated, then data accuracy is confirmed.
Given a validation failure, when detected, then the system flags it for correction.
Trust: The system logs all validation actions in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Adds a validated lifecycle status to src/lifecycle.py (approved -> validated on success, approved -> changes_requested on failure, reusing STORY-008's existing correction loop rather than a parallel one). src/data_validation_rules.py defines data accuracy deterministically: every field_binding in an approved draft solution must trace back (case-insensitive substring match) to something stated in the request's own analysis (business_objectives, scope, kpis, filters, calculations, visual_requirements, reporting_expectations) -- no model call needed. src/data_validation.py (DataValidation.validate) fetches the approved request, rejects if analysis or draft_solution is missing (MissingValidationDataError), then atomically updates status and writes one audit entry (data_validation_passed or data_validation_failed, the latter storing the joined violations in error_category) in a single transaction, same _transition shape as StakeholderReview. Wired via POST /requests/<id>/validate (src/data_validation_routes.py); a sqlite3.Error during that atomic write is caught and returned as a controlled 500 audit_log_unavailable, since this story's failure list explicitly names audit-trail logging failure as a case to handle.

Trust: The system logs all publication actions in the audit trail.
